items.name: intro_text
items.label:
Welcome

This tool scores the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 (PID-5) and its abbreviated versions and references the scores to norms for the German general population. The norms come from Zimmermann, Kerber, Kemper, and Rek (2026). They rest on a probability-based reference sample from the GESIS Panel (N = 4,727) and three donor samples that completed the full PID-5 (N = 2,471), combined through a modular Bayesian norming pipeline.

What you get:

  • percentile-based T scores for all facets and domains of the selected instrument, referenced either to the general adult population or to people of the same gender and age group,
  • for every T score a 95% credible interval for the person's true T score that combines the measurement imprecision of the instrument with the uncertainty of the norms,
  • a table and a graphical display of the profile.

What you can enter: either the responses to all items of the questionnaire or the precomputed sum scores of the facets (for the PID-5-BF and the PID5BF+M: of the domains).

Privacy: The entered values are used only to compute the results. They are not stored permanently and not passed on to third parties. Do not enter names or other identifying information.

Note: The results do not replace clinical judgment. Please read the interpretation notes on the results page.

items.name: instruction
items.label:
Questionnaire: PID-5 (220 items)

This is a list of things different people might say about themselves. We are interested in how you would describe yourself. There are no right or wrong answers, so you can describe yourself as honestly as possible. Take your time and read each statement carefully, selecting the response that best describes you.
